problem: Hilbert's sixteenth problem : what are the possible configurations of the connected components of M-curves ?
missing_details: Precise definition of an M-curve as a non-singular real algebraic curve of degree n attaining Harnack’s bound of (n²–3n+4)/2 components
Specification that curves lie in the real projective plane RP²
Quantification over every positive integer degree n
Classification up to topological equivalence (homeomorphism or isotopy) in RP²
Description of possible nesting relations among the ovals
refined_question: In the real projective plane RP², for each positive integer n, let C be a non-singular real algebraic curve of degree n whose real locus has the maximal number (n² − 3n + 4)/2 of connected components (Harnack’s bound). Determine, up to homeomorphism (or isotopy) of RP², all possible arrangements of these connected components (ovals), specifying their mutual positions and nesting structure.
justification: The Wikipedia article defines M-curves as real plane algebraic curves of degree n in RP² with exactly (n²–3n+4)/2 components and states Hilbert’s challenge to classify their component configurations (turn1view0). The problem name alone omits the ambient space (RP²), the requirement of nonsingularity, the precise bound from Harnack’s theorem, the role of the parameter n, and the need for classification up to isotopy; hence we include these details to make the question self-contained (turn2view0).
